description: AppLovin Corporation (Nasdaq: APP) provides AI-powered advertising solutions for mobile app developers and advertisers. Its principal executive offices are at 1100 Page Mill Road, Palo Alto, California, per its SEC filings. Its Axon advertising platform operates across mobile applications worldwide, reaching over one billion daily active users, and the company also operates a portfolio of its own mobile apps.
law25_relevance: Quebec businesses embedding the AppLovin SDK or buying its ads route Quebec users' device and advertising identifiers to an adtech intermediary, so the SDK, its publishers, and advertising partners must appear in the organization's data map as recipients, with the consent flow documented.
mapping_features: Its published US multistate privacy notice contains a table of personal information categories collected: identifiers such as IP address and advertising IDs (IDFA/GAID/Amazon FOSAID), email and phone identifiers, account records, and financial information, with sources (devices, publishers, advertising partners) and disclosure recipients (service providers, advertising partners, government and law enforcement).

Its MAX SDK support documentation describes a GDPR consent flow, including detecting whether a user is in a GDPR region and re-showing the consent-management-platform prompt to existing users to reset consent.
name: AppLovin Corporation
pricing_model: platform fees paid by advertisers; exact tiers unverified

law25_relevance: Arm appears in Quebec data maps mainly as a vendor of licensed software and as the operator of its website and support channels, which collect professional contact and device information from Quebec licensees and visitors.

Its Fixed Virtual Platforms end user license agreement discloses that Arm software may transmit computer information (IP address, hardware and operating system details, tool serial numbers) to Arm to verify license rights and monitor compliance.

The Dutch Data Protection Authority approved ASML's Controller Binding Corporate Rules as appropriate safeguards for intra-group personal data transfers under the GDPR.
